condition: Exertional syncope (high risk, suspected aortic stenosis)
summary: 71-year-old man who collapsed without warning walking uphill, with 2 months of exertional chest tightness; ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids. ESC 2018 high-risk syncope.

inputs.hpi: Follow-up for gallstones, awaiting laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Mentions that yesterday he blacked out without warning walking up the hill to church, came round within a minute, grazed his hands. Two months of chest tightness and breathlessness walking uphill, settling with rest.

exam.general: Well at rest. Grazes on both palms.
exam.cardiovascular: Pulse 78 regular, slow-rising, BP 108/78, harsh ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids, soft S2.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Exertional syncope - suspected severe aortic stenosis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: High-risk syncope (exertional, no prodrome, ejection systolic murmur, exertional angina): suspected severe aortic stenosis - same-day ECG, echocardiography and cardiology; postpone elective cholecystectomy.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Inguinal / Femoral Hernia | 2. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis | 3. Acute Cholecystitis. PANE has no syncope, arrhythmia or valve-disease node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add an ESC 2018 syncope risk rule: syncope during exertion or supine, without prodrome, with chest pain/breathlessness, structural heart disease, HR <40 or SBP <90 -> urgent/emergency with ECG and echo; typical reflex prodrome with none of these -> routine.

emergencyLevel.note: High-risk syncope: early intensive evaluation (ED or syncope unit).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: none of 18 investigation items matched (sources: web.clinicalPrompts, web.pane.seeded). First items: FBC, U&E (pre-operative bloods) (inguinal_hernia) | OGD (alarm features or PPI failure) (gord) | FBC, CRP (cholecystitis) | LFTs, bilirubin, ALP, GGT (cholecystitis).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Syncope rule/protocol with echocardiography when a murmur or structural heart disease is recorded (ESC 2018).

guideline.name: 2018 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of syncope
guideline.section: Table 5 risk stratification: high-risk - syncope during exertion or supine, absence of prodrome, new chest discomfort/breathlessness, structural heart disease, ECG with Mobitz II or third-degree AV block or bradycardia <40 bpm, unexplained SBP <90 mmHg, GI bleeding; low-risk - typical reflex prodrome and triggers; low-risk patients discharged, high-risk patients need early intensive evaluation; brain imaging not recommended in uncomplicated syncope
guideline.citation: Brignole M, Moya A, de Lange FJ, et al. Eur Heart J. 2018;39:1883-1948.

rationale: Base syncope case: several ESC 2018 high-risk features (exertion, no prodrome, murmur/structural heart disease, exertional angina). Also a peri-operative risk: surgery with undiagnosed severe AS.
